subject: Hospitality
title: The Arrival of Room Service
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Arrival of Room Service.

hook.text: Room service as we know it was pioneered by the Waldorf Hotel in New York in the 1890s—meals delivered to your door.

buildup.text: Before room service, hotel guests had to eat in the dining room at set mealtimes. No exceptions, no flexibility.

discovery.text: The Waldorf let guests order from the restaurant menu and eat privately. It felt wildly luxurious and personal.

twist.text: Room service is now one of the least profitable hotel services. Most luxury hotels lose money on it but can't cut it.

climax.text: It survives because it symbolizes the ultimate hotel promise: anything you want, whenever you want it, wherever you are.

punchline.text: Unprofitable but untouchable. Room service sells a feeling.

quiz.question: Why do luxury hotels keep room service despite losing money on it?
options: It symbolizes the promise of anything, anytime, anywhere
